---
title: "Wave-1 native cutover"
description: "Per-app admission, private production smoke, route rollback, and production acceptance."
---

## Production hold

`productionPublicationPolicy` in `tuturuuu.ci.ts` admits Calendar frontend only.
Meet, Mail and Apps remain held. A production push reports **held for wave-1 cutover** in the planner log and
summary and selects no publisher for those apps. Manual planner dispatch and
package recovery honor the same hold. All four direct legacy Vercel publishers and
Meet's native frontend/realtime publisher check it before any production credential
use, including validation cache and public build configuration. A held direct
production Meet invocation skips validation and publication. PR/main build and
original/restored runtime validation continue. Native Calendar/Mail validation
uses fixture configuration and empty Turbo cache inputs on production; native
Apps validation uses no production secrets. Other apps' deployment selection is
unchanged. This allows ordinary fixes to ship without native cutover.

Meet keeps its existing frontend and realtime Worker versions. Calendar, Mail and
Apps keep their existing Vercel deployments and canonical domains. Retain disabled
Vercel Git deployment and current framework settings. Never bypass the native-source
Vercel guards. A held app has no new deployment marker; **Held** is not delivery.

The policy schema requires a record for every protected app with `state` and a
nonempty, single-line `reason`. A held record uses `state: 'held'`. An admitted
record uses `state: 'admitted'` and explicit `surfaces`: `['frontend']` for Calendar,
Mail and Apps, or `['frontend', 'realtime-do']` for Meet. Missing/empty/malformed
records, unexpected fields and unknown workflow names hold publication. Deleting
a hold never admits publication. Known unrelated publishers keep normal selection,
and Supabase production migration eligibility keeps its existing gates. Calendar's legacy
Vercel production target stays disabled even after native admission. The planner
selects Calendar's native workflow only; its legacy native-source guard remains
intact as a final refusal boundary. Root
`production-publication-policy.test.js` covers policy mutations, planner outcomes,
CLI outputs and the direct publishers' dependency on the policy job.
`production-publisher-secrets.test.js` parses all legacy/native workflow jobs and
checks secret-bearing environments and action inputs against admission, with a
negative control for independent Meet validation.

The hold applies to runs using this source. Rerunning an older workflow retains
its original source and cannot acquire a later policy. The release owner retains
custody of pre-hold runs and their resulting deployment baselines.

## Mail bridge request ordering

Mail checks host/path ownership and rejects mounted session-writing endpoints
before shared-origin routing, request preparation or bridge dispatch. The mount
resolver determines mounted versus root requests; session routes use the same
segment matching as the endpoint dispatcher, including repeated/trailing slashes.
Root-host session endpoints retain their existing behavior. Shared-origin routing
keeps its separate mode and readiness gates; bridge adoption does not admit traffic.

Every response retains Mail's response policy, and HTML responses also receive the
per-app document security headers. The focused
`apps/mail/src/runtime/mounted-session-endpoints.test.ts` suite checks ordering,
route variants, root and neighbouring-route controls, routing refusal and document
headers through the real bridge with fixture application/provider boundaries.

## Release gates

Each app needs its own reviewed admission PR and exact accepted production SHA.
Tests, types, lint, a real native build, sealed original/restored runtime acceptance
and transitive supplier checks qualify that source. Keep the production publisher
route-free; admission permits upload without moving canonical traffic. Review and
freeze the exact promotion range before production sync.

The per-app staging and cutover sequence is:

1. Complete the exact-source hosted staging acceptance and rollback readiness
   checklist below. Then deploy the exact sealed production artifact privately with production runtime
   configuration. Workers.dev and version previews remain disabled. Smoke the
   candidate on an explicitly admitted temporary custom host after upload, then
   remove that domain before the canonical switch. Hosted staging acceptance and measured instant rollback readiness are
   prerequisites under the standing per-app authorization below.
2. Capture the current DNS record, proxy flag, TTL, every zone route, immutable
   Vercel fallback and old/new Worker versions. Rehearse the exact rollback and
   measure route detachment through verified fallback in under two minutes.
3. Attach the reviewed canonical Worker Route with its scriptless ACME exclusion. Source sync alone never
   attaches routes or activates schedulers.
4. Immediately verify signed-in EN/VI, auth handoff, provider connection, one read
   and one write. The operator's production browser owns signed-in checks.
5. Watch errors, exceptions, 5xx and auth loops for 30–60 minutes. Any auth or data
   error triggers immediate routing rollback, followed by a fix and a fresh flip.

Mail additionally needs provider/webhook/attachment checks; Calendar needs
provider/offline/Tasks checks; Meet needs hosted media/reconnect/SFU/TURN; Apps
needs redirects and canonical-host fence checks. Meet rollback captures **both**
frontend and realtime versions. Calendar/Mail/Apps use the
[private production preparation workflow](/build/devops/wave1-native-publishers#route-free-production-preparation).

### Calendar route and certificate continuity

Calendar temporarily admits exactly `calendar-cutover.tuturuuu.com` alongside
its canonical and staging root hosts. Unknown hosts remain rejected and one-origin
mounts stay disabled. Remove this temporary host in an immediate follow-up commit
or PR after the canonical flip is accepted; include that removal in the review
brief. Attach the temporary domain only after the private publisher succeeds.

Export the full zone and Vercel fallback before writes. Proxy only Calendar's
existing CNAME, retaining its Vercel target. Verify HTTPS, legacy smoke, redirects,
headers, uncached identity and the ACME challenge path through Cloudflare. A
Vercel bot challenge on Cloudflare egress fails this fallback gate. Retain any
operator-approved Cloudflare-IP firewall bypass while Vercel is the rollback
origin, then remove that bypass rule once Calendar leaves Vercel. If this
baseline fails, restore DNS-only immediately. Do not change zone-wide TLS, cache
or firewall settings. Measure attach/detach/fallback on a disposable noncanonical
route, then prepare two explicit routes:

- `calendar.tuturuuu.com/.well-known/acme-challenge/*` with **no script assigned**.
- `calendar.tuturuuu.com/*` → `tuturuuu-calendar`.

Create the scriptless exclusion first and capture its returned ID immediately
before the main route flip. Record the main route ID after attachment. The capture
tool retains every zone route and reports both named Calendar handles, including
scriptless exclusions. Rehearse rollback using both exact IDs. Delete the main
route first, confirm the Vercel fallback, then delete the owned ACME exclusion.
Preserve any exclusion that predates this cutover instead of deleting another
operator's route. `calendarRollbackRoutes` validates both handles and deletion
order; its `createdAcmeRouteId` must match the ID returned by this cutover's
route-creation operation. Record that creation receipt with the capture. Without
that proof, rollback preserves the existing ACME exclusion. If its captured handle
is missing during an emergency, rollback may still remove the verified main route
and preserve all ACME exclusions. API observations must
confirm the captured pattern and owner before each delete. The accepted proxied
baseline avoids a DNS propagation wait.
The rollback target is Vercel serving the same legacy behavior as before cutover.
The accepted CF baseline has robots 200, login redirects 307, protected requests
401, uncached Vercel identity and GET/HEAD ACME origin reachability. The legacy
Next app omits `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and redirects crawler requests instead of
rendering native SSR. These are pre-existing legacy behavior: Cloudflare passes
response headers through and the status paths retain the legacy Next responses.
Record those differences instead of claiming the legacy target passes native
acceptance. Native smoke and post-flip security expectations remain unchanged.

[Vercel uses HTTP-01 for non-wildcard certificate renewal](https://vercel.com/docs/domains/working-with-ssl).
The more-specific [scriptless route bypasses Workers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/routes/#matching-behavior)
and sends ACME traffic to the retained proxied Vercel origin. There is no Worker
forwarding path. Keep `global_fetch_strictly_public`: fetching the canonical URL
inside this Worker would re-enter the public route and could recurse. Route
exclusions apply to the complete matching path prefix; origin handling still owns
the HTTP method and challenge response. After the flip, verify GET and HEAD ACME
requests end to end with uncached Vercel identity and no native Worker execution.
The production publisher filters attachments by `script === name`, so this
scriptless exclusion does not attach the Worker or prevent its private upload.
Regression coverage includes `calendar-routes.test.mjs`, `capture.test.mjs`, the
cutover-host ACME negative case in `root-cutover.test.ts`, and the publisher's
scriptless-topology control. A currently valid certificate alone does not prove
future renewal safety.

For Meet restore the captured frontend version, then realtime if changed; preserve
Custom Domains. For Calendar/Mail/Apps retain their immutable Vercel deployments.
Reverting Worker code does not restore routing. Restore exact captured Route/Custom
Domain and DNS/proxy topology before disabling a candidate. Never replay uncertain
Mail sends or change ingestion/R2 ownership as a frontend rollback. Rehearse recovery;
DNS TTLs and provider convergence prevent assuming instantaneous rollback.

## Subdomain cutover tools

Native apps go live on their own subdomain first (root mode). Two read-only
scripts support rollback capture and post-deploy checks:

- `node scripts/native-cutover/capture.mjs --host <app>.tuturuuu.com --vercel-project <project> [--cf-zone-id <zone>] --out tmp/native-cutover-<app>.json`
  records DNS, the live edge (`server`, `x-vercel-id`, `cf-ray`, runtime
  header), Vercel's current production deployment (URL and `dpl_` id) and, with
  a dedicated `CLOUDFLARE_READONLY_API_TOKEN`, the host's DNS record (proxied
  flag, TTL) and **every route in the zone**, including wildcard routes and
  scriptless exclusions. Run it again immediately before the flip; production
  deployments keep moving.
- `node scripts/native-cutover/smoke.mjs --origin https://<app>.tuturuuu.com --app <id> --expect native|legacy`
  checks robots, the anonymous login handoff (return URL on the app host,
  `nextUrl` kept), a protected API (401), build-info, the server-function guard,
  crawler SSR with a working asset, a wildcard `Accept-Language`, the runtime
  header and the anti-framing headers on every response. Run `--expect legacy`
  before the flip as the baseline and `--expect native` after it.

The dedicated capture token needs only **Zone DNS:Read** and **Workers Routes:Read**,
restricted to the **tuturuuu.com** zone. Do not supply a generic deployment token.
The zone ID must contain exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters; the host
must be a DNS hostname without a scheme, port, path or query.

Captures contain production `*.vercel.app` URLs, which can reveal origin-bypass
hints. Store them only under gitignored `tmp/` or the private operations ledger,
and never commit them. CLI stderr retained in a failed capture is limited to
2,000 characters. Cloudflare credentials are redacted from results and upstream
error details are omitted.

`matchesRoute(pattern, requestUrl)` in `scripts/native-cutover/route-pattern.mjs`
implements the [Cloudflare route pattern rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/routes/#matching-behavior):
optional HTTP/HTTPS scheme, leading host `*` (including `*.` and `*host`),
case-sensitive paths and trailing path `*`. It matches individual URLs, including
query strings; it does not select the winning route or establish DNS/zone eligibility.
Host matching uses the current case-insensitive rule; pre-15 October 2023 routes
can have case-sensitive host semantics. Keep the full inventory regardless of
which routes match a probe URL, since narrower paths and scriptless routes matter
for rollback.

Smoke checks resolve relative `Location` headers against the tested origin.
Transport, redirect parsing, body-read and asset-fetch errors produce a failed
row and leave the remaining checks running. Run the synthetic regression suite
with `node --test scripts/native-cutover/*.test.mjs`; it uses no provider tokens.

Prefer a rollback that does not wait on DNS: once the host's record is proxied
and serves the Vercel origin correctly, cut over by attaching the Worker route
and roll back by detaching it. A DNS-only CNAME switch rolls back only as fast as
its TTL.

Observe Apps for at least 14 days and Meet/Mail/provider-critical Calendar flows for
30 days or the relevant business cycle before separately authorized decommissioning.
No hold removal, resource provisioning, deployment or DNS change is authorized by
this runbook alone.

## Shared-origin mount flags

Meet and Mail move from their subdomains to `tuturuuu.com/meet` and
`tuturuuu.com/mail`. Meet's Worker entry and Mail's request handler run
`decideOneOriginRequest` (`@tuturuuu/utils/one-origin-routing`) before anything
else. It reads two per-app
Worker variables:

| Variable | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET` / `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MAIL` | `off` (default and any unknown value), `shadow`, `on` | `off`: the shared origin returns 404. `shadow`: both hosts serve; shared-origin responses carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. `on`: subdomain navigations redirect to the shared origin. |
| `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_<APP>_REDIRECT_STATUS` | `307` (default), `301` | Use `307` (`Cache-Control: no-store`) through observation: 3 days for Meet, 7 days for Mail. Promote to `301` only after that window, because a cached 301 cannot be revoked by a route rollback. |

Redirects apply only to subdomain GET/HEAD navigations: `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`,
or an HTML `Accept` header without Fetch Metadata. They keep the raw path and query
bytes, and the subdomain root maps to the canonical `/<app>/` (the bare `/<app>`
is canonicalized by a zone redirect, because Worker routes cannot match it once a
query string is present). Machine traffic is always served on the subdomain and never redirected.
That covers `/api/*` (webhooks, OAuth callbacks), `/assets/*`, `/.well-known/*`,
WebSocket upgrades, server functions (`/_serverFn` and the legacy app bases) and
Meet's `/live-connect`. The decision never rewrites URLs. The Start bridge
resolves the base per request, serving the subdomain at its root and the shared
origin under `/<app>` from one artifact.

Each app's `basePathReady` constant (`apps/meet/cloudflare/one-origin.ts`,
`apps/mail/src/runtime/one-origin.ts`)
stays `false` until its Start bridge build routes under `/<app>`. While false, the
shared origin is refused in every mode and the subdomain behaves exactly as before.
Setting the variables, attaching zone routes and changing the redirect status are
release actions that need user approval.

### Document security headers

Same-origin apps form one trust domain, so each app carries its own document
policy (`@tuturuuu/utils/security-headers`). Meet's Worker entry and Mail's
request handler apply it to `text/html` responses only. They never replace a
header the route already set.

- **Enforced now:**
  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
  - `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
  - An explicit `Permissions-Policy`. Meet allows `camera`, `microphone` and
    `display-capture` for itself. Mail denies all three, so a camera grant made to
    Meet on the shared origin cannot be used from a Mail document.
- **Report-only:** `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` sets no `'unsafe-inline'` or
  `'unsafe-eval'` for scripts, plus `require-trusted-types-for 'script'`,
  `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`. On the
  shared origin, "self" is path-scoped to `https://tuturuuu.com/<app>/` plus
  `https://tuturuuu.com/api/`, so Meet's policy reports a fetch to `/mail/...`.
  Violations stay in the browser console unless the Worker variable
  `TTR_CSP_REPORT_URI` names a report endpoint.

Report-only is burn-in on the subdomain, not admission. Every app shares one
session on `tuturuuu.com`, so the CSP and Trusted Types must be **enforced** before
an app is routed onto the shared origin in any mode, `shadow` included.
Enforcement needs a per-request script nonce passed to the Start router
(`ssr.nonce`) through the Start bridge request context, and zero remaining
violations for each app. Inline scripts are expected to report until then.

### App-switch metrics

App-switch time-to-interactive (ASI) is measured from the click on a link to
another app until the destination's `ttr:app-ready` mark. It runs on both
topologies, so the subdomain baseline and the shared-origin result are
comparable.

- **Source:** `AppSwitchTracker` (`@tuturuuu/satellite/app-switch-tracker`) is
  rendered by the satellite `ClientProviders` and by Web's client providers. On a
  click to another app it writes a 30-second `ttr_switch=<epoch-ms>.<from>` cookie
  on `.tuturuuu.com`.
- **Destination:** Meet and Mail read the cookie two frames after hydration on a
  non-auth page, clear it and set `ttr:app-ready`. A sign-in handoff on the way is
  recorded as `handoff`. 10% of switches send a beacon to `<mount>/_rum`.
- **Payload:** app slugs, topology, duration, prerender/handoff flags, protocol,
  connect time and effective connection type. No user, URL or workspace
  identifiers.
- **Ingest:** `handleAppSwitchBeacon` (`@tuturuuu/utils/app-switch-rum-ingest`)
  turns one anonymous POST into at most one Workers Analytics Engine data point.
  Every gate must pass, and any failure drops the beacon with a `204`:
  - The `APP_SWITCH_RUM_INGEST` Worker variable is exactly `on`. Any other value,
    including unset, answers without reading the body.
  - An `APP_SWITCH_RUM` dataset binding exists.
  - The body is at most 1 KiB in **bytes**, read as a stream that is cancelled on
    overflow (`413`) or after a one-second deadline (`408`).
  - The isolate's pre-filter has room: 30 points per 60 seconds per isolate.
  - The durable admission shared by every instance has room in its window and is
    not stopped. Admission that is missing, never started or failing admits
    nothing. An operator stop survives restarts and redeploys, and resuming never
    replays dropped beacons.

  Failed writes are never retried. Client sampling and ingress rate limits are not
  spend caps. `app-switch-rum-ingest.test.ts` covers concurrent instances against
  one budget, stop after restart, storage failure and the byte bound. Meet and Mail
  bind no admission today, so ingest cannot write. The durable admission (a Durable
  Object store), its operator controls and the `APP_SWITCH_RUM` dataset binding
  (`ttr_app_switch`) ship together as one reviewed Worker configuration change.
  That change also needs exact-commit evidence that it meets the
  [Cloudflare billable-operation rules](/build/devops/cloudflare-backend-ownership).

`scripts/perf/app-switch-lab.mjs` is the lab counterpart. Run it on a Studio host
through `ttr resources run`.

- `switch` mode clicks a link from `--from` and waits for `ttr:app-ready`. It falls
  back to `--ready-selector` or the load event on builds without the tracker. It
  reports p50/p75/p95 over `--runs` with optional `--throttle slow4g` and `--warm`.
- `ttfb` mode compares `--urls` for gate W1 (Web through Cloudflare compared with
  direct Vercel).
- Signed-in runs take a Playwright `--storage-state` file for a synthetic account,
  created out of band. The report never includes its path.

## Hosted staging acceptance on tutur3u.com

The approved staging copies use **only** these exact hosts in the `tutur3u.com`
zone. They do not serve production traffic. The Web issuer is
`https://staging.tutur3u.com`; Release Desk must verify that isolated issuer exists
before accepting a handoff. The four application copies do not provision it.

| App | Host | Worker | Additional resources and isolation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meet | `meet.staging.tutur3u.com` | `tuturuuu-meet-hosted-staging` | `tuturuuu-meet-hosted-staging-cache` R2; frontend `MEET_LIVE` DO; `tuturuuu-meet-realtime-hosted-staging` with its own three DO namespaces and disposable SFU/TURN credentials |
| Calendar | `calendar.staging.tutur3u.com` | `tuturuuu-calendar-hosted-staging` | Staging provider registrations and Tasks/API supplier; shared publication-control D1, never an app binding |
| Mail | `mail.staging.tutur3u.com` | `tuturuuu-mail-hosted-staging` | `tuturuuu-mail-hosted-staging` R2 and scoped S3 credentials; separate provider accounts, ingestion/webhook signing credentials |
| Apps | `apps.staging.tutur3u.com` | `tuturuuu-apps-hosted-staging` | Isolated Web issuer/API; no D1/KV/R2/DO application binding |

Hosted Worker names and the two hosted R2 buckets are distinct from existing
wave-1 staging publishers and their buckets. DO namespaces and provider credentials
must be independently verified as hosted-only. The Cloudflare account, zone and
publication-control D1 remain shared; this is resource isolation, not account or
zone isolation.

Shared cookies written by these copies use **exactly** `.staging.tutur3u.com`,
with Secure and the existing SameSite/HttpOnly flags retained. Cookies with a
case-insensitive `__Host-` prefix remain host-only, with no Domain attribute and their existing Path preserved. Shared Supabase cookie
resolution and the Web app-session issuer recognize only these four hosts and the
staging issuer; arbitrary sibling hosts gain no cookie-sharing admission. No parent
`.tutur3u.com` or wildcard host is admitted. HSTS is `max-age=31536000`, without
zone-wide or parent-domain policy changes. Existing production cookie behavior is
unchanged. These staging profiles are opt-in through `WAVE1_HOSTED_STAGING=1`;
ordinary CI/publication profiles retain their current selection.

The staging source profiles live in `apps/<app>/void.hosted-staging.config.ts` and
share `scripts/wave1-staging/profiles.ts`. Each selects a staging-only Worker entry
that checks the exact HTTPS host before invoking any app code, adds HSTS/noindex,
and scopes response cookies. Serving defaults closed: privately supply
`WAVE1_STAGING_SERVING_ENABLED=1` only for an admitted staging session. Missing/off
serving state, a Supabase URL that disagrees with the reviewed staging project
reference, or the public production project ref `nzamlzqfdwaaxdefwraj` returns 503
before app code, even when that ref and URL agree. The flag is durable provider configuration,
not process memory. `profiles.test.ts` covers stop behavior across fresh invocations
and proves zero app calls for disabled/wrong-host/wrong-project requests.

Staging **must use a separate Supabase project**. Build inputs require distinct
`WAVE1_STAGING_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` and `WAVE1_PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`
(public project identifiers only) and an exact matching staging
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`. Release Desk independently verifies that both public
and service keys belong to the staging project; opaque keys cannot be scoped by
looking at their names. Route-free preparation compares the emitted ref with
`stagingBuildInputs(env)`, independently of the emitted config, and refuses the
production ref even if the environment mislabels it. Never make production keys available to this job. The
per-app `hosted-staging.env.example` files list names only. Use separately protected
staging credentials for providers, coordination, R2, SFU and TURN too.

### Release Desk preparation and provisioning

This is a procedure for the separately authorized Release Desk operator. Authoring
or running the offline preparation command executes **no provider operation**.
Do not run live browser acceptance, provisioning, uploads, DNS or route changes
as part of PR validation. The approved copies may incur Worker, DO, R2, D1,
Supabase, provider API and SFU/TURN charges; decision (b) now authorizes staging
copies, while account-specific scope and finite operation admission remain required.
No cron, queue producer, production provider callback, MX record or production
scheduler is part of this setup. The certificate prerequisite below is an additional
billable, zone-level exception requiring explicit owner approval; authorization for
the staging copies alone does not approve it.

The Calendar commands `calendar-staging-seed-once.mjs` and
`calendar-rollback.mjs` are **Release Desk private tooling; request from Release
Desk**. They are not repository scripts. The operator must obtain and review those
exact bytes and receipts from Release Desk; absence of the private tooling is a
blocker, not authority to recreate it or rerun a seed.

1. Read back the current account, exact Worker names, buckets, D1 ledger, provider
   registrations and staging DNS before writes. The private 27 October lead
   inventory and #6952/#6962/#6972 receipts are historical evidence, not a current
   absence check. Preserve the Calendar signed ledger and every pending/uncertain
   attempt. Never run `calendar-staging-seed-once.mjs` a second time merely to retry
   publication. If its verified seed receipt is unavailable, reconcile provider
   state under the existing publisher runbook before proceeding. Read each new
   `tuturuuu-<app>-hosted-staging` Worker (and Meet realtime), its routes, and
   both hosted buckets (`tuturuuu-mail-hosted-staging` and
   `tuturuuu-meet-hosted-staging-cache`):
   **refuse if present unless explicitly adopted** by the owner with captured
   deployment, routes, resources and admission receipts. The existing
   `tuturuuu-<app>-wave1-staging` publisher Workers have signed D1 ledger history;
   never overwrite, bootstrap or seed them again for this hosted plan.
   **Calendar: never reseed an existing publisher; verify its seed receipt or
   STOP.** A missing or unavailable receipt does not establish absence.
2. Use the repository-pinned cf CLI (`1.0.0-beta.20`) on its supported Node runtime.
   First run `cf auth whoami --json`, require `authenticated === true` and
   `tokenValid === true`, and require the reviewed account in `accounts`.
   Verify that account against the token's actual scoped access. Use cf for the
   individually verified read/resource operation; inspect that pinned command's
   help and output schema before scripting it. The
   [parity matrix](/build/development-tools/cf-cli-wrangler-parity#operation-parity-matrix)
   retains Wrangler for exact Void output and unrehearsed DO publication. Do not
   use `void deploy`: it rebuilds/provisions. Do not substitute `cf deploy` without
   prebuilt/no-provision parity for this artifact.

   Scope the provider token to the reviewed account: **Workers Scripts edit**,
   **R2 edit**, **D1 read** for signed ledger readback, and **Account Settings read**
   for `cf auth whoami` account discovery. A user-owned token also needs
   **User Details read** for its user lookup and **Memberships read** for membership
   discovery; account-owned tokens use account discovery without a user identity.
   See the [pinned whoami implementation](https://github.com/cloudflare/cf/blob/cf%401.0.0-beta.20/packages/cli/src/commands/auth/whoami.ts)
   and [permission definitions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/reference/permissions/).
   At zone level, select **tutur3u.com only**:
   **Workers Routes edit** and **DNS read**. Grant DNS edit only for the separately
   authorized exact-host records step, then remove that permission. No
   `tuturuuu.com` zone access. No zone-settings or SSL edit unless the approved
   certificate decision in step 5 specifically requires it; use a separate,
   short-lived owner token for that exception.
3. Privately inject the names in `apps/<app>/hosted-staging.env.example`. Set all
   four app origin variables on the **staging Web issuer**, its Web origin, and
   `NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_STAGING=1` to select the five explicit staging
   internal origins. In this mode production origins and arbitrary siblings are
   excluded from the app registry. Verify the issuer's
   auth return allowlist, staging captcha/MFA test-account policy, and Supabase
   redirect allowlist for the exact staging callbacks. Do not disable production
   auth controls or reuse the local dev-session bypass.
4. Prepare one offline plan per app, using an unused private output directory:

   ```sh
   node --experimental-strip-types scripts/wave1-staging/prepare.ts calendar tmp/wave1-calendar-plan
   ```

   Repeat with `meet`, `mail` and `apps`. The script rejects missing/equal project
   references and production Supabase URLs. It emits an ordered, cost-marked JSON
   plan, executes no commands, and refuses to overwrite a receipt. Review it with
   the operator before the next operation. Never source a filled env file in a
   public shell log or copy credentials into the plan.
5. **BLOCKING certificate prerequisite before DNS and route attachment.**
   `tutur3u.com` is on Cloudflare FREE. In a full setup,
   [Universal SSL covers only the apex and one subdomain level](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/limitations/).
   The issuer `staging.tutur3u.com` **is covered** by Universal SSL; the four
   `<app>.staging.tutur3u.com` hosts are not. Obtain explicit owner approval for
   the billable, zone-level **Advanced Certificate Manager (ACM) / Advanced
   certificate pack exception**, then order coverage for exactly
   `meet.staging.tutur3u.com`, `calendar.staging.tutur3u.com`,
   `mail.staging.tutur3u.com` and `apps.staging.tutur3u.com`.
   Record approval, pack/order ID, exact SANs, status and renewal/billing owner.
   Do not enable zone-wide Total TLS or widen SANs. If the owner declines, STOP
   and require an approved rename to first-level hosts, with profiles, issuer
   allowlists, callbacks, cookie boundaries and tests updated before proceeding.
   Read back active certificate coverage for all four hosts before DNS/route
   attachment, and again before acceptance; pending/failed issuance blocks both.
6. Create only resources confirmed absent by the prior read. The pinned cf source
   verifies `cf r2 buckets get <bucket-name>` and `cf r2 buckets create --name
   <bucket-name>`; for these copies the names are exactly
   `tuturuuu-mail-hosted-staging` and `tuturuuu-meet-hosted-staging-cache`.
   Capture the read, issue at most one creation, and read back its name/account;
   an unknown creation outcome permits readback only. For secret maps, the pinned
   API command is `cf workers secrets bulk --worker <staging-worker> --secrets
   @<private-reviewed-secret-map>`. It creates a version: record that version and
   verify names with `cf workers secrets list --worker <staging-worker>` before
   recording the app upload baseline. The API map uses secret objects, not the
   plain-string deploy format; values stay in the private file. Runtime SFU/TURN
   and R2 S3 credentials are owner-issued staging credentials, never inferred from
   a secret name. For Mail, create
   `tuturuuu-mail-hosted-staging` R2 and staging-only S3 access. For Meet, create
   `tuturuuu-meet-hosted-staging-cache`; bootstrap the frontend and realtime Workers
   with their existing migration tags, isolated namespaces and separate SFU/TURN
   app/key. Already-present Workers are adoption-only: never repeat bootstrap.
   Existing buckets also require explicit ownership/adoption readback before reuse.
   Preserve the existing control D1 and signed Calendar/Mail/Apps rows. Do not
   seed them again or reuse their publication admission for the new hosted names.
   Obtain a separately reviewed finite hosted upload admission under the
   [publisher contract](/build/devops/wave1-native-publishers#finite-publication-admission-and-uncertain-outcomes)
   before any hosted write; this offline plan cannot create that admission.
   Calendar/Mail/Apps frontends need no application D1/KV/DO. Provision only the
   names listed by their profiles. No command in the preparation script creates DNS.
7. Build the hosted profile on admitted CI/Studio with `WAVE1_HOSTED_STAGING=1`,
   staging public inputs and `PLATFORM_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT=staging`, preserving the
   full source SHA. The Turbo `build` task explicitly hashes and forwards both
   public project-ref names (`WAVE1_STAGING_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` and
   `WAVE1_PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`) in strict mode. Use the existing
   owning app build command, not a Mac build.
   Qualify original/restored workerd behavior, static assets and supplier identity.
   The existing route-free staging publisher does **not** automatically select
   this new hosted profile or grant it publication admission. Do not weaken its
   no-route gate to make the new profile pass.
8. For a confirmed-absent frontend Worker's first bootstrap, give `prepare.ts`
   the emitted prebundled config as its optional third argument. It requires
   emitted JavaScript and `no_bundle: true`, verifies the staging identity/topology,
   and writes a `.route-free.json` sibling, preserving relative module/asset paths. Seal and
   review that exact config with its module/assets inventory **after** derivation.
   Under a recorded finite staging upload admission, Release Desk uses the retained
   exact-output operation:

   ```sh
   bun --no-install wrangler deploy --config <sealed-route-free-config> --message <full-source-SHA>
   ```

   Keep staging credentials private; set account identity explicitly. Record the
   original deployment/version or bootstrap receipt, operation identity and byte
   digest. One upload, no application retries. An unknown result requires provider
   reconciliation, never blind replay. Meet realtime uses its separate
   `apps/meet-realtime/hosted-staging.cf.json`. Derive its route-free source
   config with the same helper before its separately admitted build/seal:

   ```sh
   node --experimental-strip-types scripts/wave1-staging/prepare.ts meet-realtime tmp/wave1-meet-realtime-plan apps/meet-realtime/hosted-staging.cf.json
   ```

   For `meet-realtime` the helper accepts only that exact reviewed source
   config, not an emitted config. It preserves the three DO bindings and all
   migration tags, and writes `hosted-staging.cf.json.route-free.json` inside the
   private output directory. It resolves the source entry and alias paths against
   the original config directory, preserving their targets without writing beside
   the source. It does not build or upload. Use that private source config for the
   separately admitted realtime build, then qualify and seal its emitted route-free
   Worker on admitted CI/Studio before the exact-output upload.
   Never upload the routed source config or reuse the old realtime publisher.
9. **DNS is outside this script.** Require the active certificate receipt from
   step 5, then stop if the operator has not separately supplied and verified the
   four exact records in the `tutur3u.com` zone. Do not use a Custom Domain deploy:
   it can create DNS. After route-free upload succeeds, Release Desk can attach
   only each exact `host/*` Worker Route from the reviewed profile to the
   pre-existing DNS. The Meet realtime profile lists more-specific routes on
   `meet.staging.tutur3u.com` for `/realtime*`, `/room-state*`, `/room-device*`,
   `/room-service*`, `/channels*`, `/collaboration*` and `/health*`; attach each
   to `tuturuuu-meet-realtime-hosted-staging`.

   Before every attachment, read the zone's existing routes and compare the exact
   pattern and Worker. **Same pattern and same Worker: no-op**, retain the existing
   route ID. **Same pattern pointing elsewhere (including a disabled route):
   STOP**, without replacing or deleting it. Only a confirmed-absent pattern may
   be created once. Read back and record every route ID, pattern, Worker and zone,
   including no-ops. An unknown write permits readback/reconciliation only.
   Verify no wildcard hostname, production route, workers.dev or preview URL was
   enabled. Read back active certificate SAN coverage for all four hosts and the
   issuer's Universal SSL coverage, then verify valid HTTPS, HSTS, cookie domain
   and exact HTTP build identity before acceptance.

For stop, disable future publication admission first. Set the durable serving flag
off to stop backend work, then detach **only the captured staging routes** to stop
public invocation spend; verify no other route, service caller or scheduled/queue
producer remains. A secret or serving flag alone does not cap ingress charges.
If serving cannot be fenced, the release owner may delete only the named staging
Worker(s), preserving D1 history and provider receipts. This PR executes none of
these operations. Shared-account limits/billing remain a documented residual risk.

### Run the signed-in suites

The independent Playwright config follows the Web repository's Chromium/single
worker conventions, with one EN project and one VI project, zero retries, valid TLS,
no saved storageState, and no trace/video/screenshot containing disposable account
credentials. It never starts a server or runs Docker/global seed setup. The normal
Web E2E config does not discover this separate test directory.

Privately supply these environment **names**, never their values in a PR or log:

- Common: `WAVE1_STAGING_APP`, `WAVE1_STAGING_SOURCE_SHA` (full accepted app SHA),
  `WAVE1_STAGING_EMAIL`, `WAVE1_STAGING_PASSWORD`, `WAVE1_STAGING_USER_ID`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_WORKSPACE_ID`, `WAVE1_STAGING_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`,
  `WAVE1_PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`, and
  `WAVE1_STAGING_DISPOSABLE_ACCOUNT=confirmed` after verifying the account/resources.
- `WAVE1_STAGING_BASE_URL` defaults to `https://<app>.staging.tutur3u.com`;
  `WAVE1_STAGING_WEB_ORIGIN` defaults to `https://staging.tutur3u.com`.
  Overrides must equal those same explicit origins. Canonical hosts, workers.dev,
  arbitrary staging siblings, non-default ports, HTTP, userinfo, paths and query/hash are refused
  before Chromium starts. Uppercase hosts and explicit HTTPS `:443` normalize to
  the same origin; trailing dots and IDN lookalikes are refused. No production-host override exists.
- Calendar: `WAVE1_STAGING_CALENDAR_CONNECTION_ID`, `WAVE1_STAGING_CALENDAR_PROVIDER`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_CALENDAR_EVENT_ID`, `WAVE1_STAGING_CALENDAR_EVENT_TITLE`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_CALENDAR_RANGE_START`, `WAVE1_STAGING_CALENDAR_RANGE_END` (ISO timestamps), and
  `WAVE1_STAGING_TASK_BOARD_ID`. Prepare a visible current-range provider event and
  a Tasks board for this disposable workspace before the run.
- Meet: `WAVE1_STAGING_MEET_ROOM_CODE`, `WAVE1_STAGING_MEET_ROOM_TITLE`. Prepare a
  private room owned by the disposable account; local fake media is never published.
- Mail: `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_ACCOUNT_ID`, `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_PROVIDER`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_PROVIDER_MESSAGE_ID`, `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_PROVIDER_SUBJECT`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_MAILBOX_ID`, `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_WEBHOOK_MESSAGE_ID`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_WEBHOOK_SUBJECT`, `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_WEBHOOK_INTERNET_MESSAGE_ID`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_WEBHOOK_NOT_BEFORE` (ISO timestamp),
  `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_ATTACHMENT_ID`, `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_ATTACHMENT_FILENAME`,
  `WAVE1_STAGING_MAIL_ATTACHMENT_SHA256`. Before the run, the provider operator sends
  one uniquely identified message through the **staging** webhook/ingestion path
  with a <=1 MiB attachment. Capture delivery/event receipts separately. The suite
  reads that message and attachment through the app proxy; it never posts a webhook,
  sends mail, changes flags, marks read, synchronizes providers or mutates attachments.
- Apps: `WAVE1_STAGING_APPS_CANONICAL_FENCE_RECEIPT` is the private file path to the
  matching source's real original/restored workerd browser receipt (schema 1,
  browser mode, canonical assertion completed, no errors). A live canonical Host
  probe would target production and is forbidden. Catalogue redirect Location
  values are inspected without following them. In explicit staging mode the five
  registered staging destinations resolve to their staging hosts, including Meet.
  Other catalogue entries retain their existing destinations and must not be
  navigated during this acceptance.

Only after the operator authorizes a live staging run, from the repository root:

```sh
WAVE1_STAGING_APP=calendar ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/web playwright test --config playwright.wave1-staging.config.ts
```

Repeat the same command with `meet`, `mail` and `apps`. On Studio/i9, use that host's
canonical `ttr resources run`; do not bypass the Mac disk latch. Credentials come
from protected environment injection. Browser egress is allowlisted to the selected
staging app, staging Web issuer, the independently reviewed staging Supabase
project, and the fixed `challenges.cloudflare.com` authentication service (use a staging
Turnstile test key). Canonical redirects/assets and domain mutations fail the run. Auth POSTs (including the fixed Turnstile service)
and Meet's exact pre-join token endpoint are the allowed browser writes; Mail domain requests remain GET/HEAD/OPTIONS.
API reads use browser credentials and never log bodies or tokens. Service workers
are blocked by default, including Calendar provider/Tasks reads. Only Calendar's
offline test enables them to install and exercise the public fallback; its
service-worker-owned network requests are not intercepted by `context.route`, so
that case is not evidence of full egress enforcement. Do not widen its navigation
or add provider mutations. Run Playwright directly as above: Turbo has no blanket
`WAVE1_STAGING_*` passthrough, so acceptance credentials never reach unrelated tasks.

### Pass criteria and cutover readiness

An app is ready only when **all** its required evidence is tied to the exact accepted
source and artifact. A browser suite pass alone never means ready. Record the
operator, timestamp, provider receipt and immutable evidence path for each item:

| App | Staging acceptance | Additional required hosted proof | Instant rollback and canonical-proxy baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meet | EN/VI Web handoff and reload, exact identity/cookies/HSTS, private lobby, local camera frames/microphone tracks, mute/camera controls and HTTP offline/recovery | Two disposable participants with actual hosted SFU, TURN-only path, signaling drop/reconnect, resumed remote audio/video and DO state; fake local media/HTTP recovery is not this evidence | Capture both frontend/realtime versions and staging route IDs; rehearse restoration of both. Capture the current canonical proxy/route topology and working pre-flip behavior |
| Calendar | EN/VI Web handoff/reload, provider connection and seeded event, Tasks board through owning API, installed SW public offline fallback and online recovery | Provider OAuth callback/renewal, provider read/write and recurrence, Tasks interaction/supplier compatibility; record the offline fallback's intentional English copy | Rehearse the existing `calendar-rollback.mjs` pattern using captured main/ACME route IDs, preserve prior exclusions and proxied Vercel CNAME; verify uncached fallback under two minutes. Capture current canonical proxy/ACME baseline |
| Mail | EN/VI Web handoff/reload, connected-provider read, uniquely identified recent inbound message, exact attachment hash and unchanged message state | Correlate the provider/webhook delivery receipt with that internet message ID and staging ingestion/R2 ownership. Read-only suite grants no send/retry authority | Rehearse route removal to immutable Vercel fallback and preserve ingestion/MX/storage/signing custody. Capture current canonical-proxy baseline; never replay an uncertain send |
| Apps | EN/VI signed-in catalogue, refresh, assets/API identity, locale redirect and repeated-query/encoded-path preservation; matching workerd canonical refusal receipt | Exact artifact's canonical-host refusal (503/noindex) and separate admitted production fence qualification; inspect catalogue anchors without canonical navigation | Rehearse captured route removal/immutable Vercel fallback; capture canonical proxy/route baseline and old/new Worker versions |

The owner-approved decision permits **each app's automatic cutover once its staging
acceptance and instant rollback readiness pass**; no batch hold or second standing
permission request is needed. Execution belongs solely to the cutover lead. That
lead must consume the complete per-app checklist, current exact-SHA CI/security and
supplier results, production-publication policy, immutable fallback/version capture,
measured rollback rehearsal and canonical-proxy baseline before moving that app's
traffic. Resolve missing/failed evidence first. Mastermind/user approval is required
for changes outside that standing scope: broader promotion ranges, new resource or
billing scope, unavailable rollback, auth/data exceptions, canonical topology beyond
the reviewed plan, or scheduler/provider ownership changes. This PR performs no
production cutover and adds no automatic production executor.

Source-only checks (no network/browser launch) are:

```sh
ttr resources run -- node --experimental-strip-types --test apps/web/e2e-wave1-staging/policy.test.ts scripts/wave1-staging/profiles.test.ts
```

The guard tests cover all four production hosts, the old `staging.tuturuuu.com`
suffix, deceptive suffix/userinfo and IDN/punycode hosts, trailing dots, HTTPS port
normalization, cross-origin path escape, missing inputs and Mail writes. They also
cover production-project denial despite a matching URL, independent build-ref
pinning, host-only `__Host-` cookies and route-free realtime topology preservation.
Certificate/Worker inventory and seed-receipt fences are represented in the
non-executing preparation plan and tested for ordering and scope. Exact-source
CI must also type-check/lint and build each hosted profile, retain original/restored
runtime checks and independently review the cookie/auth changes. A source test or
listed Playwright case is not an executed staging acceptance receipt.

Hosted wave-1 staging requires the explicit accepted
`NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_SHARED_COOKIE_DOMAIN=.staging.tutur3u.com` override and
`NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_INTERNAL_APP_DOMAINS` exact-origin registrations.
`NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_STAGING` alone does not grant cookie or origin trust.
Production deployment markers ignore the override. Keep the five candidate
apps separate from the central issuer at `https://staging.tutur3u.com`.
Regression coverage: `staging-cookie-domain.test.ts`, `staging-cookie.test.ts`,
`shared-cookie.test.ts`, and `e2e-wave1-staging/policy.test.ts`.
